claims.text: Brittle behavior in initially single-phase HEAs emerges primarily when local chemical ordering or clustering develops at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary ordering or clustering can induce embrittling phases or disrupt an entropy-stabilized matrix.
Brittleness in these HEAs is not primarily caused by the conventional grain-boundary segregation or precipitation mechanisms found in traditional alloys.
High configurational entropy suppresses rapid grain coarsening.
High configurational entropy suppresses intermetallic precipitation.
Certain thermal or mechanical loading conditions can produce local chemical ordering at grain boundaries.
Local chemical ordering reduces configurational entropy locally.
Reduced local configurational entropy can trigger brittle grain-boundary features.
Intermediate-temperature annealing or cyclic deformation can induce grain-boundary ordering or clustering without changing the overall phase composition.
Grain-boundary ordering or clustering can generate short-range-ordered regions, nanoscale precipitates, or depleted zones.
Brittle grain-boundary features act as crack-initiation sites.
Brittle grain-boundary features reduce toughness even in the absence of conventional grain-boundary precipitation or segregation.
Treatments that promote local ordering or clustering will decrease Charpy impact energy or fracture toughness relative to the initial single-phase HEA.
Treatments that promote only conventional grain-boundary segregation or precipitation will not decrease HEA toughness.
The toughness loss in an HEA will be less severe than in conventional alloys subjected to similar treatments.
The toughness decrease will correlate with evidence of local ordering at grain boundaries.
The proposed initial single-phase HEA baseline has high toughness and no grain-boundary embrittlement or precipitation.
A conventional-alloy baseline would show rapid toughness loss upon grain-boundary precipitation.
The mechanism applies to compositionally complex, entropy-stabilized alloys with initially single-phase microstructures and fails when conventional precipitation dominates.

contradictions.description: The intervention is specified to induce ordering without changing overall phase composition, while the mediator and hypothesis allow formation of nanoscale precipitates or embrittling phases. Formation of a distinct precipitate phase conflicts with strict retention of a single-phase state unless 'overall phase composition' is intended only to exclude detectable bulk phase changes.
